title: Brigham City v. Stuart (2006)
key_points: Holding: Officers may enter a home without a warrant when they have an objectively reasonable basis to believe an occupant is seriously injured or imminently threatened.
New Jersey: See State v. Edmonds, 211 N.J. 117 (2012): the emergency-aid entry needs an objectively reasonable basis and the scope is limited to the emergency.
officer_notes: Scenario: Through a window you see a fight in a kitchen and a teen punch an adult, who spits blood.
Takeaway: Document what you saw or heard that showed an emergency.
